# setup
```{r}
# this code chunk should be copied everywhere
library(tidyverse)

# loading in data
sal <- read_csv(paste0(
  "https://stat.cmu.edu/~sgallagh/courses/mads-fall-2026/",
  "datavis-36613/data/salaries.csv.gz"
))

# Order experience levels by seniority
sal$experience_level <- factor(
  sal$experience_level,
  levels = c("EN", "MI", "SE", "EX"),
  labels = c("Entry", "Mid", "Senior", "Executive")
)

# Create work arrangement variable
sal <- sal |> 
  mutate(
    remote = case_when(
      remote_ratio == 0 ~ "On-Site",
      remote_ratio == 50 ~ "Hybrid",
      remote_ratio == 100 ~ "Fully remote"
    ), 
    remote = factor(
      remote,
      levels = c("On-Site", "Hybrid", "Fully remote")
    )
  )

# Keep only full-time positions
sal <- sal |> 
  filter(employment_type == "FT") |> 
  mutate(
    log_salary = log(salary_in_usd)
  )
```


# graph split by seniority level
```{r}
# Salary density plot
ggplot(
  sal,
  aes(
    x = salary_in_usd,
    fill = remote,
    color = remote
  )
) +
  
  geom_density(
    alpha = 0.25,
    linewidth = 0.9
  ) +
  
  scale_x_log10(
    labels = scales::label_dollar(
      accuracy = 10000
    )
  ) +
  
  facet_wrap(
    ~ experience_level,
    nrow = 1
  ) +
  
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "On-Site" = "#4C78A8",
      "Hybrid" = "#F2CF5B",
      "Fully remote" = "#59A14F"
    )
  ) +
  
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "On-Site" = "#4C78A8",
      "Hybrid" = "#F2CF5B",
      "Fully remote" = "#59A14F"
    )
  ) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Salary Distributions by Work Arrangement and Experience",
    subtitle = "Salary distributions are shown on a logarithmic scale within each experience level.",
    x = "Annual salary (USD)",
    y = "Density",
    fill = "Work arrangement",
    color = "Work arrangement",
    caption = "A higher density within the graph indicates a larger concentration of salaries at that salary level. 
    Experience levels are ordered by seniority, from entry level to company executives."
  ) +
  
  theme_classic(base_size = 13) +
  
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 17
    ),
    
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 11,
      color = "gray30"
    ),
    
    axis.title = element_text(
      face = "bold"
    ),
    
    axis.text = element_text(
      color = "gray20"
    ),
    
    strip.background = element_rect(
      fill = "gray95",
      color = NA
    ),
    
    strip.text = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 11
    ),
    
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(
      color = "gray90",
      linewidth = 0.4
    ),
    
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    
    legend.title = element_text(
      face = "bold"
    ),
    
    plot.caption = element_text(
      hjust = 0,
      color = "gray40",
      size = 9
    )
  )



```

# boxplot graph

```{r}
# Label remote variable
sal <- sal |> 
  mutate(
    remote = case_when(
      remote_ratio == 0 ~ "On-Site",
      remote_ratio == 50 ~ "Hybrid",
      remote_ratio == 100 ~ "Fully remote"
    ), 
    remote = factor(
      remote,
      levels = c("On-Site", "Hybrid", "Fully remote")
    )
  )


# Boxplot of salary by work arrangement
ggplot(
  sal,
  aes(x = remote, y = salary_in_usd, fill = remote)
) +
  
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.55,
    alpha = 0.75,
    outlier.alpha = 0.15,
    outlier.size = 1
  ) +
  
  # Show median as a white point
  stat_summary(
    fun = median,
    geom = "point",
    shape = 21,
    size = 3,
    fill = "white"
  ) +
  
  # Logarithmic y-axis
  scale_y_log10(
    breaks = c(
      10000,
      30000,
      50000,
      100000,
      200000,
      300000,
      500000
    ),
    labels = scales::label_dollar(
      accuracy = 1000
    )
  ) +
  
  # Colors
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "On-Site" = "#4C78A8",
      "Hybrid" = "#F2CF5B",
      "Fully remote" = "#59A14F"
    )
  ) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Salary Distributions by Work Arrangement",
    subtitle = "Median salaries are approximately $148K for on-site, $70K for hybrid, and $145K for \nfully remote roles",
    x = "Work arrangement",
    y = "Annual salary (USD)",
    caption = "Note: Salaries are displayed on a logarithmic scale to improve a viewer's understanding of comparison across 
    wide salary ranges.") +
  
  theme_classic(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 17
    ),
    
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 11,
      color = "gray30"
    ),
    
    axis.title = element_text(
      face = "bold"
    ),
    
    axis.text = element_text(
      color = "gray20"
    ),
    
    plot.caption = element_text(
      hjust = 0,
      color = "gray40",
      size = 9
    ),
    
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(
      color = "gray90",
      linewidth = 0.4
    ),
    
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```
